answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with the reputation it claims, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Peers then attest only work they can independently verify, like a cedar's rings recording slow, costly growth: a jade seal of approval is earned over time, not minted at will. When an identity is caught cheating, its stake is slashed to its nadir and its attestations are revoked, making fraud unprofitable at scale while honest agents keep compounding trust.
